correctness.rationale: Exact support h(u)=a√(x²+y²)+b√(y²+z²)+c√(z²+x²). Concavity on squared-normal simplex proves radius b+c; tight ±e_z fixes all optimal centers to z=0. For a nonvertical normal, the reduced barrier involves Φ_q(ρ)=qρ/[1+√(1−qρ²)], monotone for q∈[0,1], so horizontal normals are necessary and sufficient. Their inequalities are exactly membership in a rectangle plus a positive Euclidean disk, or erosion by a disk of radius b+c−a. Explicit side lengths yield the complete locus and planar area; derivatives give 2π−8 at the switch. The standalone finite checker passes 12 parameter cases and validates boundary/exterior clearance with sampled normals. No finite sampling is substituted for analytic sufficiency.

value.rationale: Provides the entire family of centers of maximal Euclidean balls in a natural three-disc zonoid, including tied-weight lower-dimensional regimes. The global positive-weight classification identifies a sharp additive rectangle-to-rounded-rectangle transition and universal loss of twice differentiability in center-area, independent of already known circumradius contact phases. This is a substantial full metric locus, not merely a radius restatement, arbitrary parameter slice or code-only observation.
